prompts.text: What game did we play at home that you wish younger relatives still knew?
Tell me about a rainy afternoon when the family invented its own entertainment.
We're planning a games afternoon using only things found around the house. What should we include?
Bring back a childhood board game or teach everyone an old playground game?
The rules of family games often change depending on who remembers them.
A homemade game sometimes becomes a stronger family memory than an expensive toy.
Who in the family was famous for making up rules halfway through a game?
Describe a game that ended with everyone laughing more than competing.
A younger cousin asks us to teach a game from our childhood. How do we explain it without arguing over the rules?
Which childhood game would surprise you if you found out our relatives still play it?
What part of a normal school day felt like the biggest adventure when you were little?
Tell me about a teacher whose unusual teaching method stayed with you.
We each bring one object to a family gathering that reminds us of school. What would you choose?
Revisit an old classroom or walk around the playground you remember?
The little routines around school sometimes stay in our memories longer than the lessons.
Two siblings can remember the same school very differently.
What school lunch or snack would immediately remind you of being a child?
Describe the first time you felt proud of learning something on your own.
A child in the family asks what school was like before smartphones. What detail would you explain first?
Which school tradition would you want to bring back for one day?
What's the funniest detail you've noticed in an old photograph of our family?
Tell me about a family photograph whose backstory is more interesting than the picture.
We find an unlabelled album. Who would be the best person to help identify everyone?
Sort old pictures by year or arrange them around the stories people remember?
The things in the background of family photographs often reveal how childhood has changed.
An imperfect family photograph often tells a better story than a carefully posed one.
Which childhood haircut or outfit would you enjoy seeing everyone react to again?
Describe a picture that reminds you of a family tradition we no longer follow.
A younger relative sees an old family picture and asks about the place. What story would you tell?
What's one childhood moment you wish someone had photographed?
What did our neighbourhood have when you were young that children today might not recognise?
Tell me about a familiar street or corner that felt enormous when you were small.
We take a family walk through an old neighbourhood. Which stop should come first?
Visit an old playground or return to a shop you remember from childhood?
Children often remember the smallest landmarks in a neighbourhood most vividly.
A short walk can feel like a long journey when you're seeing the world at a child's height.
What sound from your childhood street would you recognise instantly?
Describe a neighbour who helped make the area feel like a community.
A young cousin asks where you spent most of your afternoons. How would you describe the place?
Which childhood route do you think you would still remember without directions?
Which meal made an ordinary childhood day feel special in our family?
Tell me about a cooking task you were trusted with for the first time.
We want to recreate a meal from our childhood. Whose memory of the recipe should we ask first?
Bring back a favourite homemade snack or prepare a full Sunday meal from years ago?
The stories told around a meal sometimes matter more than the food itself.
Children often remember who served a dish as clearly as how it tasted.
What ingredient did you dislike as a child but enjoy now?
Describe a family meal that turned into an unexpected celebration.
A younger relative wants to help prepare an old family recipe. Which step would be fun to teach?
What kitchen smell reminds you most strongly of growing up?
What harmless competition between siblings or cousins became a family tradition?
Tell me about a time the younger children surprised the older ones with a clever idea.
We organise a reunion activity for cousins who grew up in different places. How would we help them connect?
Retell an old cousins' adventure or recreate a favourite childhood group photo?
Cousins who see each other only at holidays sometimes develop their own traditions.
Family nicknames deserve an explanation before we pass them on to the next generation.
Which cousin or sibling was the organiser of all the childhood activities?
Describe a small act of kindness between siblings that you still remember.
Two relatives disagree about who started a childhood prank. How should the family settle the story?
What did you learn from growing up alongside relatives with different personalities?
Which childhood celebration felt especially magical because of the way our family prepared?
Tell me about a birthday or holiday when something unplanned became the highlight.
We recreate a childhood celebration using today's budget. Which detail matters most?
Make decorations by hand or revive an old family party game?
A celebration's familiar rituals often matter more to children than expensive presents.
A family celebration looks different when you remember it as a child rather than as an adult.
What song or greeting signalled the start of a special day at home?
Describe the first time you helped prepare for a family celebration.
A younger relative wants to know why we observe a particular tradition. Who has the best story?
Which old celebration tradition would you enjoy teaching the next generation?
What childhood possession would you be surprised to find still stored in the family home?
Tell me about a toy or book you cared for long after you stopped using it.
We're making a small display of family childhood objects. Which three items would tell the best stories?
Keep an old school notebook or a favourite childhood game?
The most meaningful childhood keepsakes often have little monetary value.
An ordinary object becomes interesting when someone explains how they used it years ago.
What did you collect as a child, and what happened to the collection?
Describe receiving a hand-me-down that you treasured more than something new.
A younger family member finds an unfamiliar old gadget. How would you demonstrate what it did?
What childhood object do you think future generations will struggle to identify?
What's a useful skill an older relative taught you when you were little?
Tell me about learning something practical by watching a family member at work.
We have an afternoon to teach children a skill we learned at home. What should we choose?
Learn a traditional hand skill or hear the story behind a family proverb?
Children remember lessons more easily when they get to try the task themselves.
A simple household chore sometimes becomes a child's first lesson in responsibility.
What question did you ask repeatedly as a child because nobody gave a satisfying answer?
Describe an adult who encouraged your curiosity instead of dismissing it.
A young relative asks how people solved everyday problems before the internet. What example would you share?
What childhood lesson do you understand differently now that you're older?
What's a childhood story about our parents or grandparents you would like to hear in more detail?
Tell me about an older relative describing a game you had never heard of.
We get an hour to record family memories. What would you ask first to make the conversation comfortable?
Hear about childhood holidays from an elder or learn what their ordinary weekdays looked like?
Everyday memories deserve as much attention as the dramatic stories families usually repeat.
Older relatives sometimes remember tiny details from childhood with surprising clarity.
What part of an older relative's childhood feels most different from your own?
Describe hearing a family story that changed how you understood someone's personality.
Two elders remember the same childhood event differently. How would you preserve both versions?
What question about growing up would you like every generation of our family to answer?
